target.title: fix(openrouter): bound music SSE buffering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:**
  OpenRouter music generation streaming in `extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.ts`, specifically the SSE reader that accumulates audio and transcript deltas from `/chat/completions` responses.
- **Root cause, in product terms:**
  Root cause: the OpenRouter music SSE parser treated the external stream as trustworthy because it assumed every event would be newline-delimited soon and every audio/transcript delta would stay reasonably sized. Pending text was appended into an in-memory string until a newline arrived, while decoded audio buffers and transcript chunks were collected without cumulative byte accounting at the source of accumulation.
- **Why it matters / User impact:**
  A malformed or oversized OpenRouter stream could make an OpenClaw process retain unbounded memory before the stream completed or timed out, instead of failing with a clear provider error.
- **Fix classification:**
  Root-cause defensive bound on untrusted provider stream accumulation.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Complete shipped solution:**
  Added byte accounting at each accumulation point: a 2 MiB pending SSE event limit before appending decoded text, a 64 MiB cumulative decoded audio limit, and a 1 MiB cumulative transcript limit.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:**
  This fixes the root parser invariant because each guard is placed at the exact source of untrusted accumulation: raw bytes are counted before SSE text is appended to the pending line buffer, decoded audio bytes are counted before a buffer is retained, and transcript UTF-8 bytes are counted before a transcript chunk is retained. The fix therefore enforces the stream-size contract where memory growth originates instead of masking the symptom later at concat time or waiting for a timeout.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:**
  The limits are local OpenRouter music-provider stream safety constants. They do not change the plugin SDK contract, request schema, auth flow, model routing, or OpenRouter wire format.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:**
  Out of scope / unchanged: this PR does not change prompt construction, reference image handling, supported music models, output formats, provider configuration, auth, model routing, request schema, or non-music OpenRouter behavior. The change is only the local OpenRouter music stream safety boundary.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:**
  Valid streams under the caps continue to behave as before. Streams exceeding the caps now fail closed with explicit OpenRouter music generation errors.
- **Risk labels considered:**
  merge-risk:compatibility due to newly enforced fail-closed caps on very large provider streams.
- **Risk explanation:**
  The main behavior change is rejection of very large OpenRouter music responses: more than 64 MiB decoded audio, more than 1 MiB transcript text, or more than 2 MiB in a single unterminated SSE event.
- **Why acceptable:**
  These caps prevent unbounded memory growth from an external stream while preserving the existing API surface and normal chunked SSE behavior. The exact thresholds are intentionally provider-local safety bounds rather than SDK contract changes.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:**
  Receive deterministic provider failures for oversized or malformed OpenRouter music streams instead of exposing the process to unbounded buffering.
- **Existing behavior preserved:**
  Normal streaming audio chunks still concatenate in order, transcript chunks still join into lyrics, `[DONE]` still ends the stream, and existing reader cleanup behavior is preserved.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:**
  My local network exit remains unable to complete OpenRouter audio generation because OpenRouter returns provider HTTP 403 (`This model is not available in your region`) for the audio-output models I tested. However, PR comment proof from `zhangguiping-xydt` successfully ran the PR head through the real OpenRouter music provider path with `google/lyria-3-pro-preview`, MP3 output, and a non-empty audio track, so the changed SSE reader path now has successful live behavior evidence.
## Evidence

- **Environment:**
  Windows 10 / Git Bash workspace for deterministic regression tests. Live OpenRouter proof was then supplied in PR discussion by `zhangguiping-xydt` from macOS Darwin 25.5.0, Node v24.15.0, OpenClaw PR head `7aa5793571`, using a funded OpenRouter API key redacted from output.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  Deterministic regression command:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --project extension-providers extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.test.ts`

  Live proof command shape from the PR comment, with the API key supplied only by environment and omitted from output:
  `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<redacted> node --import tsx openrouter-music-live-proof.ts`
- **Key results / observations:**
  The focused OpenRouter music provider test command exited 0 after the final rebase onto current `origin/main`. The regression coverage includes: unterminated SSE event over 2 MiB, cumulative decoded audio over 64 MiB across multiple SSE events, and transcript text over 1 MiB.

  Public PR comment live proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101488#issuecomment-4912411421

  The live proof ran the real `buildOpenRouterMusicGenerationProvider().generateMusic()` path with `google/lyria-3-pro-preview`, requested MP3 output, and returned a non-empty audio track. This exercises the patched `readOpenRouterAudioStream()` path because `generateMusic()` only returns after the OpenRouter SSE reader completes and produces audio.

  Redacted live output from the PR comment:

  ```text
  [live-proof] starting generateMusic model=google/lyria-3-pro-preview format=mp3 durationSeconds=5 instrumental=true
  [live-proof] success model=google/lyria-3-pro-preview
  [live-proof] returned track bytes=601040 mime=audio/mpeg file=track-1.mp3 sha256=a033077f7a6a8cfe71c51ac910dd533d55d2f34db3b0345606ed90feec96431e
  [live-proof] lyrics count=0 totalBytes=0
  ```

  Focused regression result from the same PR comment:

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  11 passed (11)
  Duration  3.51s
  ```
- **Review findings addressed, if any:**
  ClawSweeper requested real OpenRouter proof. PR comment proof from `zhangguiping-xydt` now provides redacted successful live output from a real OpenRouter music generation on PR head `7aa5793571`, and the comment explicitly requested `@clawsweeper re-review`.

  RF-001: Addressed by the public PR comment live proof, which includes redacted terminal output from a real OpenRouter music generation after this patch.
  RF-002: Addressed by the successful live `generateMusic()` call with `google/lyria-3-pro-preview`; the provider returned a non-empty MP3 audio track after the patched SSE reader completed.
  RF-003: Addressed with successful live output under the new caps: returned audio bytes were 601040, transcript/lyrics bytes were 0, and the focused regression tests still cover over-cap failure behavior.
  RF-004: Addressed by successful live proof, so a proof waiver is no longer the only available path.
  RF-005: The remaining action is ClawSweeper/maintainer re-review of the added successful proof, not a code repair still pending in this PR.
- **Regression guardrail:**
  Regression test plan: the focused provider test file adds three stream-parser tests for the exact memory-growth paths. One test feeds an SSE event that never emits a newline and exceeds 2 MiB, one test sends multiple valid SSE audio events whose cumulative decoded audio exceeds 64 MiB, and one test sends transcript data exceeding 1 MiB. These unit regression tests are the smallest reliable guardrail because they exercise `readOpenRouterAudioStream`/`processOpenRouterSseLine` deterministically without depending on external model availability.
- **Patch quality notes:**
  Diff is limited to `extensions/openrouter/music-generation-provider.ts` and its provider test file. No lockfiles, generated files, or unrelated formatting changes are intended. Patch quality warning review: the added `catch` blocks preserve the existing reader cleanup lifecycle by cancelling/releasing the stream on error; they do not swallow provider errors or convert them into fallback/default success. Related PR scan: #98351 touches OpenRouter provider parsing but only guards malformed JSON; it does not address SSE pending bytes, cumulative decoded audio, or transcript caps.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:**
  High for the targeted memory-safety fix based on deterministic current-head stream tests and confirmed `origin/main` overlap checks. Live generation success remains unavailable from my current OpenRouter region, so the fail-closed caps need maintainer acceptance or maintainer-side live proof from an allowed region.
